/* Resistance port (v141): the full barrier (PPC sync) as a locked no-op
* read-modify-write of the stack top -- what Linux uses for smp_mb() on
* x86-64. Same StoreLoad ordering for ordinary memory as mfence, at a
* fraction of the cost on Zen 2; the game's job-list helpers
* (func_005290DC & co., ~7% of the main thread) run one per call.
* PPU_FENCE_MFENCE=1 at build time keeps mfence. */
extern uint8_t* const vm_base;   /* v163: set once at boot, before any lifted code runs */
/* v163: the bounds as immediates (main.cpp maps the full space, ppu_vm_size
* = 0xE0000000; the gcm ref-poll word is ppu_hle_inject_base 0x20000000 +
* 0x2008 -- main.cpp checks both at boot). No global loads per access. */
/* v163: the out-of-line accessors behind a preserve_most wrapper
* (ppu_loader.cpp): the rare slow path no longer clobbers the caller's
* registers, so the fast path keeps its values in registers. */
extern unsigned char* const g_spu_coh_bitmap_p;   /* v163: set statically, never changes */
extern volatile int g_spu_coh_stack;              /* v163: an SPU reserved a PPU-stack line */
/* v163 (Resistance port): unchecked accessors for accesses the lifter-output
* post-pass (tools/ppu_fastmem.py) proved ordinary: stack (R_1), TOC (R_2) and
* TOC-derived constant-pool (R_30) addresses. These can never be the null
* page, raw-SPU MMIO, the gcm ref-poll word or past the end of the VM, so the
* span / poll / store-ok tests and the out-of-line fallback -- whose call
* forced spills around every access -- are dropped. Stack stores skip the SPU
* reservation bitmap too (no SPU job reserves PPU stack lines; spu_coherency.c
* logs it if one ever does -- then build with -DPPU_STACK_COH). PPU_NO_FASTMEM
static inline uint8_t  vm_read8_fast (uint64_t a) { return vm_base[(uint32_t)a]; }
static inline uint16_t vm_read16_fast(uint64_t a) { uint16_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base + (uint32_t)a, 2); return __builtin_bswap16(v); }
static inline uint32_t vm_read32_fast(uint64_t a) { uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base + (uint32_t)a, 4); return __builtin_bswap32(v); }
static inline uint64_t vm_read64_fast(uint64_t a) { uint64_t v; memcpy(&v, vm_base + (uint32_t)a, 8); return __builtin_bswap64(v); }
static inline int vm_stk_coh_hit(uint32_t ea, uint32_t n)
/* v163: no check at all. An SPU reservation on a PPU stack line would need
* one; spu_coherency.c logs "[coh] SPU reservation on a PPU stack line"
* if that ever happens (build with -DPPU_STACK_COH then). */
if (__builtin_expect(!g_spu_coh_stack, 1)) return 0;   /* no SPU has reserved a stack line */
const uint32_t l0 = ea >> 7, l1 = (ea + n - 1) >> 7;
static inline void vm_write8_stk(uint64_t a, uint8_t v)
{ const uint32_t ea = (uint32_t)a; if (__builtin_expect(vm_stk_coh_hit(ea, 1), 0)) { (vm_write8)(a, v); return; } vm_base[ea] = v; }
static inline void vm_write16_stk(uint64_t a, uint16_t v)
{ const uint32_t ea = (uint32_t)a; if (__builtin_expect(vm_stk_coh_hit(ea, 2), 0)) { (vm_write16)(a, v); return; }
static inline void vm_write32_stk(uint64_t a, uint32_t v)
{ const uint32_t ea = (uint32_t)a; if (__builtin_expect(vm_stk_coh_hit(ea, 4), 0)) { (vm_write32)(a, v); return; }
static inline void vm_write64_stk(uint64_t a, uint64_t v)
{ const uint32_t ea = (uint32_t)a; if (__builtin_expect(vm_stk_coh_hit(ea, 8), 0)) { (vm_write64)(a, v); return; }
